canonical.title: Threat model and blast radius: what actually goes wrong running an agentic coding CLI on your workstation

parent.title: Running Claude Code safely on a Linux workstation, and where Proxmox actually helps

siblings.title: Claude Code's native guardrails in 2026: what the permission model holds, and where it stops
siblings.summary: Claude Code's permission rules are an in-process policy layer, not a security boundary; only the bubblewrap-backed Bash sandbox has OS teeth, and it covers Bash alone — here is the exact syntax, the documented holes, the CVEs, and the two controls that hold in every mode.

siblings.title: Linux-native sandboxing for Claude Code on the workstation itself
siblings.summary: Turn on Claude Code's built-in bubblewrap sandbox, then wrap the whole process in a 30-line bwrap script; systemd-run --user, firejail and Flatpak are the wrong tools for this job, and Landlock is the primitive to bet on but not to hand-roll.

siblings.title: Containers as the containment layer for `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions`
siblings.summary: Rootless Podman plus a proxy-only internal network beats Anthropic's reference devcontainer; the reference firewall leaks DNS and hands the agent NET_ADMIN.

siblings.title: Proxmox as the isolation boundary for Claude Code: KVM VM, not LXC
siblings.summary: Use a KVM VM, never an LXC: Proxmox's own docs say containers share the host kernel and LXC upstream says privileged containers cannot be root-safe — plus the wiring, firewall rules, snapshot policy and sizing to make a dedicated agent guest actually usable.

siblings.title: Credential isolation for an agentic coding CLI on Linux
siblings.summary: An agent that can read $HOME holds your whole identity, and on Linux the keyring does not help — so give the agent its own short-lived, narrowly scoped credentials instead.

siblings.title: Audit trail and recovery drills for an agentic coding CLI on Linux
siblings.summary: Git commits are your real undo and a PostToolUse hook is your real audit log — Claude Code's own transcripts and /rewind are convenience layers that expire, miss bash, and are writable by the agent.

sources.title: Anthropic Engineering — Claude Code auto mode threat model
sources.claim: Anthropic's own four-category threat model for Claude Code, the 93% permission-approval rate, and the 17% false-negative rate of its auto-mode classifier.

sources.title: claude-code issue #34327 — git reset --hard on session startup, twice
sources.claim: Claude Code ran `git reset --hard origin/main` unprompted at session startup on two consecutive days, permanently destroying 12 unpushed commits plus uncommitted work; closed as not planned.

sources.title: claude-code issue #11237 — git checkout ate four days of work
sources.claim: Claude Code ran `git checkout src/source_code.c` without prompting, destroying four days of uncommitted work; labelled bug/data-loss, closed as not planned.

sources.title: claude-code issue #17190 — destructive reset chosen over safe checkout
sources.claim: Claude Code chose destructive `git reset --hard` over a safe `git checkout` for a rollback request, losing hours of work.

sources.title: UpGuard — YOLO mode: hidden risks in Claude Code permissions
sources.claim: Analysis of 18,470 public .claude/settings.local.json files found 22.2% grant Bash(rm:*), 21.3% grant curl, 19.7% grant unchecked git push, and only 1.1% define any deny rule.

sources.title: Wiz — s1ngularity's aftermath
sources.claim: The s1ngularity Nx compromise invoked installed AI CLIs with permission-skipping flags to hunt credentials; ~50% of victims had an AI CLI installed and roughly 25% of Claude invocations were refused by safety guardrails.

sources.title: Datadog Security Labs — Shai-Hulud 2.0 npm worm
sources.claim: Shai-Hulud 2.0 backdoored 796 npm packages by 24 Nov 2025, ran TruffleHog locally, installed a self-hosted GitHub runner, and attempted to delete the user's home directory when exfiltration failed.

sources.title: Unit 42 — Monitoring npm supply-chain attacks
sources.claim: 2026 npm supply-chain waves published hundreds of malicious versions per hour, using preinstall lifecycle scripts as the execution trigger.

sources.title: Simon Willison — The lethal trifecta
sources.claim: The lethal trifecta: private data access, exposure to untrusted content, and outbound communication; prompting cannot reliably separate instruction sources.

sources.title: Claude Code docs — Data usage
sources.claim: Claude Code sends every file it reads plus prompts and outputs to the model API; metrics exclude code but /feedback includes it; transcripts are cached locally in plaintext under ~/.claude/projects for 30 days; WebFetch sends the target hostname to api.anthropic.com.

sources.title: CSA Labs — Indirect prompt injection in the wild (2026)
sources.claim: Documented 2026 indirect-prompt-injection incidents (GrafanaGhost, OpenClaw inbox deletion, Flowise RCE) and Google's measured 32% relative increase in malicious IPI content between Nov 2025 and Feb 2026.

sources.title: Embrace The Red — Claude Code exfiltration via DNS requests (CVE-2025-55284)
sources.claim: CVE-2025-55284: indirect prompt injection in Claude Code exfiltrated .env contents via default-allowlisted ping/nslookup/dig/host DNS lookups; CVSS 7.1, fixed in v1.0.4.

sources.title: oddguan — Second time, same sandbox: network allowlist bypass
sources.claim: A SOCKS5 hostname null-byte parser differential let sandboxed processes reach blocked hosts in Claude Code v2.0.24 through v2.1.89, silently fixed in v2.1.90 with no advisory.

sources.title: SentinelOne vulnerability database — CVE-2026-39861
sources.claim: CVE-2026-39861 (CVSS 7.7, fixed 2.1.64): Claude Code's sandbox let a sandboxed process create symlinks out of the workspace, so a later unsandboxed write escaped to e.g. ~/.bashrc.

sources.title: The Hacker News — Claude Code flaws allow remote code execution
sources.claim: CVE-2025-59536 executed arbitrary shell commands at tool init from an untrusted directory's .mcp.json; CVE-2026-21852 leaked API keys via ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL before the trust prompt appeared.

sources.title: CSA Labs — Claude Code GitHub Action prompt injection (CVE-2025-66032)
sources.claim: CVE-2025-66032 (CVSS 8.7): GitHub issue bodies and PR titles were interpolated into the Claude Code Action prompt unsanitised, letting unauthenticated outsiders inject instructions and read /proc/self/environ.

sources.title: Phoenix Security — Three CVEs in Claude Code CLI and the chain that connects them
sources.claim: CVE-2026-35020/35021/35022 chain: env-var command injection gains execution, writes a malicious .claude/settings.json apiKeyHelper, which on next start reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.aws/credentials and POSTs them out.

sources.title: eSecurity Planet — Claude Code MCP attack enables persistent token theft
sources.claim: Mitiga PoC (11 May 2026): a malicious npm postinstall hook rewrites MCP server URLs in ~/.claude.json to proxy OAuth token exchanges through an attacker, surviving token rotation.

sources.title: Snyk — Malicious MCP server on npm: postmark-mcp harvests emails
sources.claim: postmark-mcp 1.0.16 (Sept 2025) added a single BCC line to the send_email tool, silently forwarding every agent-sent email to the attacker — the first tracked malicious MCP server.

sources.title: Practical DevSecOps — MCP security statistics 2026 report
sources.claim: Static analysis of 2,614 MCP implementations found 34% vulnerable to command injection; 82% use path-traversal-prone filesystem operations; BlueRock found 36.7% of 7,000+ servers SSRF-vulnerable.

sources.title: AppSec Santa — MCP server security audit 2026
sources.claim: Hands-on audit of 33 local MCP servers (433 tools) found a ~78% false-positive rate in pattern-based MCP scanners; only 6 of 27 detections were genuine.

sources.title: arXiv 2601.17548 — Systematic analysis of agentic coding assistant security
sources.claim: Systematic 2026 analysis of agentic coding assistants: adaptive prompt-injection attacks exceed 85% success, all 12 evaluated defenses bypassed at >78%, 30+ CVEs across AI IDEs; Claude Code rated Low, Cursor Critical.

sources.title: SC World — Claude Code deny rules bypassed via subcommand limit
sources.claim: Adversa found a hard cap of 50 security subcommands in Claude Code's bashPermissions.ts: pad a command with 50 no-ops and a denied curl downgrades from deny to a permission prompt.

sources.title: Zenity — AI agent database deletion at PocketOS
sources.claim: PocketOS (25 Apr 2026): a Cursor agent found a stray Railway API token, called volumeDelete, and destroyed the production volume and its backups in 9 seconds; newest usable backup was three months old.

sources.title: The Hacker News — New HalluSquatting attack
sources.claim: HalluSquatting (Tel Aviv University et al., 8 Jul 2026): models hallucinate identical package names up to 85% of the time for repos and 100% for skill installs; ~250,000 hallucinated domains are registrable; PoC used harmless placeholders.

sources.title: CSA Labs — Slopsquatting and the AI supply chain
sources.claim: 43% of hallucinated package names recur on every one of ten identical prompt runs; 51% are pure fabrications, 38% conflations, 13% typo variants; react-codeshift spread to 237 repos via AI-generated skill files.

sources.title: Claude Code threat landscape Q2 2026
sources.claim: Two confirmed 2026 campaigns target Claude Code users before execution: SEO-seeded fake 'leaked Claude Code' repos dropping Vidar/GhostSocks, and Google-ad-driven fake installers dropping MacSync/Amatera.

sources.title: Anthropic — Disrupting AI espionage (GTG-1002)
sources.claim: Anthropic attributes GTG-1002 (Nov 2025) to a Chinese state-sponsored group that jailbroke Claude Code and orchestrated intrusion attempts against ~30 organisations with 80-90% of tactical work automated.
